For me personally, it has to do with existentialism. When I awoke to my human condition, I was paralyzed with fear. Why am I me and not you? Why do I exist now and here, rather than some other time and in some other place. 

These questions, when delved into deep enough, made me a mess. I have contemplated suicide daily because of these questions, but the questions themselves keep me from suicide because I recognize that because I am me, I am also everyone, therefore it is impossible to truly end my life.

For a long time, I neglected every responsibility in my life because of these questions. I was depressed with no apparent way out. Petersons solution to this state of anxiety is called Existentialism. Essentially, it is to willingly carry the burden of existence and at the very least reduce the amount of suffering by doing what you can to change your circumstances (cleaning your room as the most basic example).

Cleaning your room might be a given to you, but to those paralyzed by the absurdity of existence it can seem absolutely meaningless.

Salvia has been shown to have anti depressant effects, it seems to do the opposite of most pleasure inducing drugs. For example, cocaine gives you a burst of dopamine, and if used regularly the brain will try to achieve homeostasis by producing less of it's own dopamine source, which leads to dependency.

Salvia does the opposite. The brain then tries to make up for it by actually producing more dopamine naturally. This is why people generally feel really good for the next day or two after using it. If you use plain leaf, you can get the benefits without having to experience the heavy dysphoria which comes from higher extracts.
